newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Up gingerly on crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Up gingerly on crude gains.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps rose marginally late Wednesday, tracking the recovery in crude, brokers said.
July paper was last quoted at $23.50/$23.65, up from its morning quotes at $23.25/$23.45 and up from a day-earlier $22.90/$23.10.
A flurry of trades saw July gas oil swaps done at between $23.48-$23.55 a barrel. August was traded at $23.65.
August gas oil swaps however eased about five cents from earlier quotes and were last indicated at $23.65/$23.80.
This placed the jet/gasoil spread or regrade to $0.70/$0.90, compared to $0.80/$1.00 on Tuesday.
July regrade was traded at 27 cents.
The July jet/gas oil regrade was unchanged at $0.20/0.40.
Prompt IPE Brent futures rebounded from hitting a one-year low of $17.45 and were traded at around $17.62, helping improve sentiment in Singapore.
In the cash market, traders were still cautious.
Prompt physical gas oil was traded on Tuesday at $22.90 per barrel, the lowest in nearly a year. A Japanese trading house purchased a 150,000 barrels lifting June 25-29 cargo from a major.
Traders said prices were likely to stabilise and consolidate around this level. Most were optimistic that prices would recover in the near term.
Fuel oil swaps also recovered with firmer sentiment sparked off by gains in crude futures. July was indicated at $98.50/$99.75, about 50 cents up from its morning indications.
